notes.decision: Translated as 'throne' = Greek θρόνος. Confirmed by line 12 spelling ⲫⲣⲟⲛⲟⲥ which preserves the rho. The sequence describes the cosmic thrones of the great divine beings: Great King of Honor in the 7th firmament, Judge of Truth in the air, Apostle in the holy Church — all standard Manichaean cosmological figures who occupy specific cosmic seats.

Translated 'the sixth' (= ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲟⲟⲩ). The sequence demands an ordinal: line 1 X-th throne in the 2nd Ship, line 2 7th throne in 7th firmament, line 4 8th throne in air, line 8 9th throne in church. Line 12 confirms 'these are the [nine] great thrones.' ⲧⲧⲓⲥⲁⲩ thus = 'the sixth,' a non-standard Lyc form perhaps with article ⲧ- + ⲧⲓⲥⲁⲩ (= ⲡⲥⲟⲟⲩ '6').

'The Great King of Honor' — standard Manichaean cosmological figure who occupies the seventh (highest) firmament. ⲡⲛⲁⲃ = ⲛⲟϭ 'great' (in glossary as 'great' / ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲃ 'lordship'); ⲛ̄ⲣⲡⲟ = 'of king(s)' (cf. ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ 'reign'); ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ = 'honor.'

'The Judge of Truth' (κριτὴς τῆς ἀληθείας) — standard Manichaean cosmological figure stationed in the air, who judges human souls after death and divides them into three paths (death, life, agreement) as line 7 specifies.

Translated 'to the agreement' / 'to joining.' ⲡⲧⲱⲧ from ⲧⲱⲧ 'be joined' — already in glossary as 'the agreement / accord.' In the standard Manichaean post-mortem schema: souls go either to Light (ⲡⲱⲛⲍ 'life'), to Hell (ⲡⲙⲟⲩ 'death'), or to a third middle state — for catechumens, often described as 'reconciliation' or 'mixing.' 'Agreement' preserves the verbal-joining root.
'The ninth.' Final element ϯⲥ = ⲯⲓⲥ '9.' Confirmed by line 12 [ⲡϯⲥ] 'the nine.'

'The apostle who has come to our feet at this time' — i.e. Mani himself, the present apostolic incarnation. ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧⲧⲏⲛⲉ uses the idiom ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'unto the feet of' (in glossary) with -ⲧⲏⲛⲉ 'us' (Lyc 1pl). The 9th throne is thus the present Manichaean Church itself, with Mani as its enthroned Judge of Righteousness.
Variant spelling of ⲡⲉϫⲉϥ 'he said' (cf. ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ in glossary as Lyc 'he said'). Standard discourse-introducer in Kephalaia.

'That of the wind, that of the fire, and that of the water' — the three garments of the Living Spirit. ⲧⲁ- is the relational prefix (the-one-of). The triad wind/fire/water is the cosmological-elemental triplet by which the Living Spirit clothes himself for cosmic ordering, distinct from the five light elements.

Translated 'he subjected them' / 'he ordered them.' Likely Lyc reflex of ⲍⲱⲣⲡ̄ 'subject' or ϩⲣⲃ-related form. Context: after setting up all the works of the cosmos above and below, he then 'arranged/ordered' them. Tentative.

ⲕⲁⲕϥ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ = ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁϩⲏⲩ 'strip naked.' The damaged subject ⲡⲧ.. likely begins ⲡⲧⲏⲩ 'the wind' (first of the three garments donned in line 21) — fitting the elemental action: the wind strips the cosmos. Confidence on the subject is moderate.

Tentative. Possibly = ⲥⲱϩⲙ̄ 'rebuke' (cf. glossary ⲥⲉⲍⲙ̄) or ⲥⲁϩⲛⲉ 'command, ordain.' Context — after scattering them for purification — fits a verb of commanding or instructing. Translation 'he commanded' offered tentatively but rendered in coptic field unchanged.
'The X of the Zone.' ⲧⲁⲡ likely = 'tip, horn, edge, limit' (cf. Sah. ⲧⲁⲡ 'horn'). The zodiacal/cosmic Zone (already in glossary) has limits/tips/horns. Translated 'limits of the Zone.'
